title: plate-novae
description:
This repository searches the Harvard DASCH plates (about 1890 to 1990) for earlier eruptions of known novae, which would show that a nova is recurrent.

Status: pilot, claimed, not peer reviewed. No person outside the project has checked it.

A pilot on five stars reports, as claimed and not checked by a person, that 5 of 17 known eruptions of T Pyx, U Sco and RS Oph from 1890 to 1989 were recovered (6 of 17 with a fainter quiet level). An RS Oph signal in March 1914 is an unverified flag, not a discovery.

As DASCH asks: This work has made use of data provided by Digital Access to a Sky Century @ Harvard (DASCH), which has been partially supported by NSF grants AST-0407380, AST-0909073, and AST-1313370. Work on DASCH Data Release 7 received support from the Smithsonian American Women's History Initiative Pool.

Raw DASCH light curves are not redistributed here and are not in the archive. The scripts fetch them.

Directed by Ahraz Arifuddin

Researched and verified by different model families across Gemini, Claude, Grok, OpenAI, and Muse
